mathlib.name: T0Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A T₀ space, also known as a Kolmogorov space, is a topological space such that for every pair
`x ≠ y`, there is an open set containing one but not the other. We formulate the definition in terms
of the `Inseparable` relation. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T0Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Two inseparable points in a T₀ space are equal. -/
  t0 : ∀ ⦃x y : X⦄, Inseparable x y → x = y

mathlib.name: T1Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A T₁ space, also known as a Fréchet space, is a topological space
  where every singleton set is closed. Equivalently, for every pair
  `x ≠ y`, there is an open set containing `x` and not `y`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T1Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- A singleton in a T₁ space is a closed set. -/
  t1 : ∀ x, IsClosed ({x} : Set X)

mathlib.name: T2Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A T₂ space, also known as a Hausdorff space, is one in which for every
  `x ≠ y` there exists disjoint open sets around `x` and `y`. This is
  the most widely used of the separation axioms. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T2Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Every two points in a Hausdorff space admit disjoint open neighbourhoods. -/
  t2 : Pairwise fun x y => ∃ u v : Set X, IsOpen u ∧ IsOpen v ∧ x ∈ u ∧ y ∈ v ∧ Disjoint u v

P000004.note: pi-base T2.5 = Urysohn = disjoint closed neighborhoods; matches Mathlib T25Space. Distinct from P000009 Functionally Hausdorff (separation by a continuous function).

mathlib.name: T25Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A T₂.₅ space, also known as a Urysohn space, is a topological space
  where for every pair `x ≠ y`, there are two open sets, with the intersection of closures
  empty, one containing `x` and the other `y` . -/
mathlib.signature:
class T25Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Given two distinct points in a T₂.₅ space, their filters of closed neighborhoods are
  disjoint. -/
  t2_5 : ∀ ⦃x y : X⦄, x ≠ y → Disjoint ((𝓝 x).lift' closure) ((𝓝 y).lift' closure)

P000005.note: Mathlib T3Space = RegularSpace + T0Space, i.e. regular Hausdorff.

mathlib.name: T3Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A T₃ space is a T₀ space which is a regular space. Any T₃ space is a T₁ space, a T₂ space, and
a T₂.₅ space. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T3Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends T0Space X, RegularSpace X

instance (priority := 90) instT3Space [T0Space X] [RegularSpace X] : T3Space X := ⟨⟩

mathlib.name: T35Space
mathlib.docstring: /-- A T₃.₅ space is a completely regular space that is also T₀. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T35Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends T0Space X, CompletelyRegularSpace X

instance T35Space.instT3space [T35Space X] : T3Space X where

mathlib.name: T4Space
mathlib.docstring: /-- A T₄ space is a normal T₁ space. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T4Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends T1Space X, NormalSpace X

instance (priority := 100) [T1Space X] [NormalSpace X] : T4Space X := ⟨⟩

mathlib.name: T5Space
mathlib.docstring: /-- A T₅ space is a completely normal T₁ space. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T5Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends T1Space X, CompletelyNormalSpace X

theorem Topology.IsEmbedding.t5Space [TopologicalSpace Y] [T5Space Y] {e : X → Y}
    (he : IsEmbedding e) : T5Space X where
  __ := he.t1Space
  completely_normal := by
    have := he.completelyNormalSpace
    exact completely_normal

mathlib.name: T6Space
mathlib.docstring: /-- A T₆ space is a perfectly normal T₀ space. -/
mathlib.signature:
class T6Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends T0Space X, PerfectlyNormalSpace X

-- see Note [lower instance priority]
/-- A `T₆` space is a `T₅` space. -/
instance (priority := 100) T6Space.toT5Space [T6Space X] : T5Space X where

P000011.note: Mathlib RegularSpace does not assume T0; matches pi-base 'Regular' (P5 = T3 adds T0).

mathlib.name: RegularSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is called a *regular space* if for any closed set `s` and `a ∉ s`, there
exist disjoint open sets `U ⊇ s` and `V ∋ a`. We formulate this condition in terms of `Disjoint`ness
of filters `𝓝ˢ s` and `𝓝 a`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class RegularSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- If `a` is a point that does not belong to a closed set `s`, then `a` and `s` admit disjoint
  neighborhoods. -/
  regular : ∀ {s : Set X} {a}, IsClosed s → a ∉ s → Disjoint (𝓝ˢ s) (𝓝 a)

mathlib.name: CompletelyRegularSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A space is completely regular if points can be separated from closed sets via
  continuous functions to the unit interval. -/
mathlib.signature:
class CompletelyRegularSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  completely_regular : ∀ (x : X), ∀ K : Set X, IsClosed K → x ∉ K →
    ∃ f : X → I, Continuous f ∧ f x = 0 ∧ EqOn f 1 K

mathlib.name: NormalSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is said to be a *normal space* if any two disjoint closed sets
have disjoint open neighborhoods. -/
mathlib.signature:
class NormalSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Two disjoint sets in a normal space admit disjoint neighbourhoods. -/
  normal : ∀ s t : Set X, IsClosed s → IsClosed t → Disjoint s t → SeparatedNhds s t

mathlib.name: CompletelyNormalSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space `X` is a *completely normal space* provided that for any two sets `s`, `t`
such that if both `closure s` is disjoint with `t`, and `s` is disjoint with `closure t`,
then there exist disjoint neighbourhoods of `s` and `t`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class CompletelyNormalSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- If `closure s` is disjoint with `t`, and `s` is disjoint with `closure t`, then `s` and `t`
  admit disjoint neighbourhoods. -/
  completely_normal :
    ∀ ⦃s t : Set X⦄, Disjoint (closure s) t → Disjoint s (closure t) → Disjoint (𝓝ˢ s) (𝓝ˢ t)

mathlib.name: PerfectlyNormalSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space `X` is a *perfectly normal space* provided it is normal and
closed sets are Gδ. -/
mathlib.signature:
class PerfectlyNormalSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends NormalSpace X where
    closed_gdelta : ∀ ⦃h : Set X⦄, IsClosed h → IsGδ h

mathlib.name: R0Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is called an R₀ space, if `Specializes` relation is symmetric.

In other words, given two points `x y : X`,
if every neighborhood of `y` contains `x`, then every neighborhood of `x` contains `y`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class R0Space (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- In an R₀ space, the `Specializes` relation is symmetric. -/
  specializes_symmetric : Symmetric (Specializes : X → X → Prop)

mathlib.name: R1Space
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is called a *preregular* (a.k.a. R₁) space,
if any two topologically distinguishable points have disjoint neighbourhoods. -/
mathlib.signature:
class R1Space (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  specializes_or_disjoint_nhds (x y : X) : Specializes x y ∨ Disjoint (𝓝 x) (𝓝 y)

P000016.note: pi-base Compact = quasi-compact (no Hausdorff); matches Mathlib CompactSpace.

mathlib.name: CompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- Type class for compact spaces. Separation is sometimes included in the definition, especially
in the French literature, but we do not include it here. -/
mathlib.signature:
class CompactSpace : Prop where
  /-- In a compact space, `Set.univ` is a compact set. -/
  isCompact_univ : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set X)

mathlib.name: SigmaCompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A σ-compact space is a space that is the union of a countable collection of compact subspaces.
  Note that a locally compact separable T₂ space need not be σ-compact.
  The sequence can be extracted using `compactCovering`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class SigmaCompactSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- In a σ-compact space, `Set.univ` is a σ-compact set. -/
  isSigmaCompact_univ : IsSigmaCompact (univ : Set X)

mathlib.name: LindelofSpace
mathlib.docstring: /-- X is a Lindelöf space iff every open cover has a countable subcover. -/
mathlib.signature:
class LindelofSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- In a Lindelöf space, `Set.univ` is a Lindelöf set. -/
  isLindelof_univ : IsLindelof (univ : Set X)

mathlib.name: CountablyCompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is countably compact if every countably generated proper filter has a
cluster point. -/
mathlib.signature:
class CountablyCompactSpace (E : Type*) [TopologicalSpace E] : Prop where
  isCountablyCompact_univ : IsCountablyCompact (Set.univ : Set E)

P000023.note: pi-base 'Weakly locally compact' = each point has one compact neighborhood.

mathlib.name: WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- We say that a topological space is a *weakly locally compact space*,
if each point of this space admits a compact neighborhood. -/
mathlib.signature:
class WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Every point of a weakly locally compact space admits a compact neighborhood. -/
  exists_compact_mem_nhds (x : X) : ∃ s, IsCompact s ∧ s ∈ 𝓝 x

P000130.note: Mathlib LocallyCompactSpace = basis of compact neighborhoods (the strong form).

mathlib.name: LocallyCompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- There are various definitions of "locally compact space" in the literature,
which agree for Hausdorff spaces but not in general.
This one is the precise condition on X needed
for the evaluation map `C(X, Y) × X → Y` to be continuous for all `Y`
when `C(X, Y)` is given the compact-open topology.

See also `WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace`, a typeclass that only assumes
that each point has a compact neighborhood. -/
mathlib.signature:
class LocallyCompactSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- In a locally compact space,
  every neighbourhood of every point contains a compact neighbourhood of that same point. -/
  local_compact_nhds : ∀ (x : X), ∀ n ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ s ∈ 𝓝 x, s ⊆ n ∧ IsCompact s

mathlib.name: ParacompactSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is called paracompact, if every open covering of this space admits a locally
finite refinement. We use the same universe for all types in the definition to avoid creating a
class like `ParacompactSpace.{u v}`. Due to lemma `precise_refinement` below, every open covering
`s : α → Set X` indexed on `α : Type v` has a *precise* locally finite refinement, i.e., a locally
finite refinement `t : α → Set X` indexed on the same type such that each `∀ i, t i ⊆ s i`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class ParacompactSpace (X : Type v) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Every open cover of a paracompact space assumes a locally finite refinement. -/
  locallyFinite_refinement :
    ∀ (α : Type v) (s : α → Set X), (∀ a, IsOpen (s a)) → (⋃ a, s a = univ) →
      ∃ (β : Type v) (t : β → Set X),
        (∀ b, IsOpen (t b)) ∧ (⋃ b, t b = univ) ∧ LocallyFinite t ∧ ∀ b, ∃ a, t b ⊆ s a

P000036.note: pi-base 'Connected' = 'no disjoint nonempty open cover' = preconnected; pi-base DEDUCES the empty space (S000163) is connected, so the faithful match is PreconnectedSpace, NOT Mathlib's ConnectedSpace (which bundles Nonempty). Verified 2026-07-02 via faithfulness review + closure.

mathlib.name: PreconnectedSpace
mathlib.docstring: /-- A preconnected space is one where there is no non-trivial open partition. -/
mathlib.signature:
class PreconnectedSpace (α : Type u) [TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- The universal set `Set.univ` in a preconnected space is a preconnected set. -/
  isPreconnected_univ : IsPreconnected (univ : Set α)

P000037.note: pi-base 'Path connected' = 'every two points joined by a path'; the empty space satisfies this vacuously and pi-base deduces it path-connected. Mathlib PathConnectedSpace bundles Nonempty, so we use the bare joined-condition for faithfulness.
P000037.expr: ∀ x y : X, @Joined X i x y

mathlib_refs.name: Joined
mathlib_refs.docstring: /-- The relation "being joined by a path". This is an equivalence relation. -/

mathlib.name: LocallyConnectedSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is **locally connected** if each neighborhood filter admits a basis
of connected *open* sets. Note that it is equivalent to each point having a basis of connected
(not necessarily open) sets but in a non-trivial way, so we choose this definition and prove the
equivalence later in `locallyConnectedSpace_iff_connected_basis`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class LocallyConnectedSpace (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- Open connected neighborhoods form a basis of the neighborhoods filter. -/
  open_connected_basis : ∀ x, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun s : Set α => IsOpen s ∧ x ∈ s ∧ IsConnected s) id

P000042.note: Locally path connected. (Mathlib master renamed this to LocallyPathConnectedSpace; the pinned v4.32.0-rc1 uses LocPathConnectedSpace.)

mathlib.name: LocPathConnectedSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is locally path connected, at every point, path connected
neighborhoods form a neighborhood basis. -/
mathlib.signature:
class LocPathConnectedSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- Each neighborhood filter has a basis of path-connected neighborhoods. -/
  path_connected_basis : ∀ x : X, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun s : Set X => s ∈ 𝓝 x ∧ IsPathConnected s) id

mathlib.name: TotallyDisconnectedSpace
mathlib.docstring: /-- A space is totally disconnected if all of its connected components are singletons. -/
mathlib.signature:
class TotallyDisconnectedSpace (α : Type u) [TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- The universal set `Set.univ` in a totally disconnected space is totally disconnected. -/
  isTotallyDisconnected_univ : IsTotallyDisconnected (univ : Set α)

mathlib.name: TotallySeparatedSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A space is totally separated if any two points can be separated by two disjoint open sets
covering the whole space. -/
mathlib.signature:
@[mk_iff] class TotallySeparatedSpace (α : Type u) [TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- The universal set `Set.univ` in a totally separated space is totally separated. -/
  isTotallySeparated_univ : IsTotallySeparated (univ : Set α)

P000039.note: pi-base 'Hyperconnected' = 'no disjoint nonempty opens' = preirreducible; pi-base deduces the empty space hyperconnected, so the faithful match is PreirreducibleSpace, NOT Mathlib's IrreducibleSpace (which adds Nonempty).

mathlib.name: PreirreducibleSpace
mathlib.docstring: /-- A preirreducible space is one where there is no non-trivial pair of disjoint opens. -/
mathlib.signature:
class PreirreducibleSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  /-- In a preirreducible space, `Set.univ` is a preirreducible set. -/
  isPreirreducible_univ : IsPreirreducible (univ : Set X)

mathlib.name: ExtremallyDisconnected
mathlib.docstring:
/-- An extremally disconnected topological space is a space
in which the closure of every open set is open. -/
mathlib.signature:
class ExtremallyDisconnected : Prop where
  /-- The closure of every open set is open. -/
  open_closure : ∀ U : Set X, IsOpen U → IsOpen (closure U)

mathlib.name: DiscreteTopology
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is discrete if every set is open, that is,
  its topology equals the discrete topology `⊥`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class DiscreteTopology (α : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- The `TopologicalSpace` structure on a type with discrete topology is equal to `⊥`. -/
  eq_bot : t = ⊥

mathlib.name: MetrizableSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is metrizable if there exists a metric space structure compatible with the
topology. To minimize imports, we implement this class in terms of the existence of a
countably generated uniformity inducing the topology, which is mathematically
equivalent.
To endow such a space with a compatible uniformity, use
`letI : UniformSpace X := TopologicalSpace.pseudoMetrizableSpaceUniformity X`.
To endow such a space with a compatible distance, use
`letI : MetricSpace X := TopologicalSpace.metrizableSpaceMetric X`. -/
mathlib.signature:
class MetrizableSpace (X : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace X] : Prop extends
    PseudoMetrizableSpace X, T0Space X

-- See note [lower instance priority]
attribute [instance 100] MetrizableSpace.toT0Space
attribute [instance 100] MetrizableSpace.toPseudoMetrizableSpace

instance (priority := 100) PseudoMetrizableSpace.toMetrizableSpace

mathlib.name: PolishSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A Polish space is a topological space with second countable topology, that can be endowed
with a metric for which it is complete.

To endow a Polish space with a complete metric space structure, do
`letI := upgradeIsCompletelyMetrizable α`.
-/
mathlib.signature:
class PolishSpace (α : Type*) [h : TopologicalSpace α] : Prop
    extends SecondCountableTopology α, IsCompletelyMetrizableSpace α

instance [TopologicalSpace α] [SeparableSpace α] [IsCompletelyMetrizableSpace α] :
    PolishSpace α := by

mathlib.name: SecondCountableTopology
mathlib.docstring: /-- A second-countable space is one with a countable basis. -/
mathlib.signature:
class _root_.SecondCountableTopology : Prop where
  /-- There exists a countable set of sets that generates the topology. -/
  is_open_generated_countable : ∃ b : Set (Set α), b.Countable ∧ t = TopologicalSpace.generateFrom b

mathlib.name: FirstCountableTopology
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A first-countable space is one in which every point has a
  countable neighborhood basis. -/
mathlib.signature:
class _root_.FirstCountableTopology : Prop where
  /-- The filter `𝓝 a` is countably generated for all points `a`. -/
  nhds_generated_countable : ∀ a : α, (𝓝 a).IsCountablyGenerated

mathlib.name: SeparableSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A separable space is one with a countable dense subset, available through
`TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense`. If `α` is also known to be nonempty, then
`TopologicalSpace.denseSeq` provides a sequence `ℕ → α` with dense range, see
`TopologicalSpace.denseRange_denseSeq`.

If `α` is a uniform space with countably generated uniformity filter (e.g., an `EMetricSpace`), then
this condition is equivalent to `SecondCountableTopology α`. In this case the
latter should be used as a typeclass argument in theorems because Lean can automatically deduce
`TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace` from `SecondCountableTopology` using
`TopologicalSpace.SecondCountableTopology.to_separableSpace`, but deducing
`SecondCountableTopology` from `TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace` requires more assumptions.
-/
mathlib.signature:
@[mk_iff] class SeparableSpace : Prop where
  /-- There exists a countable dense set. -/
  exists_countable_dense : ∃ s : Set α, s.Countable ∧ Dense s

mathlib.name: BaireSpace
mathlib.docstring:
/-- The property `BaireSpace α` means that the topological space `α` has the Baire property:
any countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense.
Formulated here when the source space is ℕ.
Use `dense_iInter_of_isOpen` which works for any countable index type instead. -/
mathlib.signature:
class BaireSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  baire_property : ∀ f : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (f n)) → (∀ n, Dense (f n)) → Dense (⋂ n, f n)

mathlib.name: NoetherianSpace
mathlib.docstring: /-- Type class for Noetherian spaces. It is defined to be spaces whose open sets satisfies ACC. -/
mathlib.signature: abbrev NoetherianSpace : Prop := WellFoundedGT (Opens α)

P000090.note: Arbitrary intersections of opens are open.

mathlib.name: AlexandrovDiscrete
mathlib.docstring:
/-- A topological space is **Alexandrov-discrete** or **finitely generated** if the intersection of
a family of open sets is open. -/
mathlib.signature:
class AlexandrovDiscrete (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] : Prop where
  /-- The intersection of a family of open sets is an open set. Use `isOpen_sInter` in the root
  namespace instead. -/
  protected isOpen_sInter : ∀ S : Set (Set α), (∀ s ∈ S, IsOpen s) → IsOpen (⋂₀ S)
